lines.text: You'll be the new owner. God bless you, son.
Ah, the new owner. You're very welcome.
Morning to you, new owner. I'm Father Walsh.
The new owner. My door's open, any hour.
Welcome to the Hook, new owner. It grows on a man.
Good evening, new owner. You've had a long road.
The new owner, is it? Come in out of the cold.
New owner, you're soaked. Come under my umbrella.
Ah, the new owner. I'm glad you've come.
Mr Nowak. God bless you.
Good morning, Mr Nowak. I hope you slept.
Mr Nowak. If you've a minute, I've a kettle.
Mr Nowak. How are you settling, son?
Afternoon, Mr Nowak. The chapel's open, if you've need.
Mr Nowak. I've said a prayer for the office.
Evening, Mr Nowak. Home before the damp sets in.
Mr Nowak. Come in under the umbrella.
Mr Nowak, you're welcome here any hour.
Mr Nowak. Come to the chapel hall for tea.
Frank. God keep you.
Morning, Frank. I hope you slept.
Frank, son. Are you all right? Truly?
Frank. You needn't tell me where you've been.
Evening, Frank. The dark's no friend, son.
Frank. I'll light a candle for you, if you'd not mind.
Afternoon, Frank. A quiet hour. A good one.
Frank, you're drenched, son. Take the umbrella.
Frank, son. Is there anything I can do?
Frank. It's good to see you walking about.
Frankie, son. It's good to see you.
Frankie. You'd tell me if it was heavy, would you?
Morning, Frankie. God bless the day.
Frankie, son. Come and take the weight off.
Evening, Frankie. I've kept a chair for you.
Frankie. It keeps till morning, whatever it is.
Frankie. You're always welcome. That never changes.
Frankie, mind the damp, now.
Frankie, son. You've been in my prayers.
Ah! God help us. Mind the old bones.
Easy, son. These old legs go from under me.
Dear me. That's my glasses gone.
Sorry, sorry. Whose fault was that?
Careful, son. The pavement's older than both of us.
Steady, steady. Nobody's hurt.
Excuse me, son. We'd best both look up.
Ah, it's yourself. No harm done.
A soft day, thank God. A soft day.
Ah, here's the rain. It's only water.
And me with no umbrella. God help me.
There now. The sky's had enough.
God send it's not heavy.
Only a mist, now. It'll not trouble us.
A fine soft rain. The kind that feeds the grass.
Ah, that's a downpour. In we go.
Lord, listen to that.
Rain on the chapel roof. It's the sound of the place.
The old gutters are singing again.
It rains on the just and the unjust, they say.
Mind the puddles, son. They hide the deep ones.
Ah, the damp. It gets into the old hymn books.
A soft day, this. A good day for thinking.
Misty and mild. I'll not complain.
It's a hard rain. We'll be glad of a dry floor.
The streets will be rivers by evening.
What in the name of God was that?
That didn't sound like a lorry, son.
Lord, somebody's in trouble.
I'll go and see. Slowly, mind.
That's glass, I fear. And a good deal of it.
Stay where you are, son. Let it quieten.
I'll say a prayer. And then I'll telephone.
I'll tell the guards. Somebody should.
Somebody hurried past, God forgive me. I couldn't say who.
A shape by the wall, son. That's all I'd swear to.
Somebody ran. I'd not like to guess.
My eyes are tired. A figure, and then none.
Something moved. A person, I'd say. No more.
I'll not guess at what I didn't see.
A figure. In a hurry. God keep them.
A back, son, going away from me. No more.
God gave me a good look at that face, son.
A face I'll remember, God forgive me.
Stop, now! I saw you! God sees you too!
I've no name. I've the face, and a prayer.
I looked into that face, son. It looked back.
I'll not forget that face. I'll say a prayer for it.
That's a face I'll carry, son. I'll say no more.
That face was frightened, or angry. I couldn't tell.
Quietly, now, son. Quietly.
I'll say nothing till I know more.
Come away. There's nothing for us here.
Whoever it was, God help them.
A quiet tongue never started a quarrel.
I'll not carry this about. Not here.
We'll pray on it, and then we'll see.
Speak low. The street has ears.
I'm sorry, son. I've only ever walked the parish.
Try the cab office, son. A map on every wall.
It's beyond my parish, I'm afraid.
I'd take you myself, but I've a call to make.
Try the newsagent's. They know everyone's road.
God forgive me, I'd only send you wrong.
Is it near the chapel? Then I know.
The woman on the radio at Mickey's knows every road.
God keep you.
Go in peace, son.
Go carefully.
My door's open. Remember that.
God bless, now.
Walk safe, son.
Mind the wet, now.
Mind the dark, son. God keep you.
